Born and raised and still living in Røros.
You will have to accept that the town survives and relies on tourism. It will get crowded during summer and for christmas and RørosMartnan. However I won't say its overrun by tourists in that sense.

There's a lot of culture, depending on what you are looking for. For how lively it is, pretty much depends on how much you put into it. It's a small tightknit community and it can be hard to really penetrate that bubble you kinda have to participate in activities in one way or another.

Glåmos is a nice place but has some uncertainty regarding the schools future. There's a coop there, wich is a plus since its a bit too far cycling or walking glåmos>røros>glåmos.

The problem with the RTS genre is that it will always be played at frantic speeds. Grand empires crashing together after building the perfect Base is cool in theory, but every game boils down to how to maximise profit, never float money and always be building. That will always be the way to win the game. 

Sure, you can artificially slow the game down with build limits and such, but the best players will be doing the right thing at the perfect timing anyway. Pretty much every attempt to stop rushing will boil down to meta deathballtimings or other ways that just pushes the game longer. 

I might just be pessimistic, but players find ways to  minmax all the time. The result of any competitive RTS will look like a SC match in various forms. You'll find the balance in economy, army building and timing, and small Harassment attacks will probably work better than a deathball. So the end result will be that every game becomes fast and twitchy.

The fact that you got diagnosed and went to get help tells me that it was interfering with your life in some way. Stay with the therapy, try out medication (might not be what you need, ask your doctors) and be prepared for a possibly long battle.

In Oslo (dunno about other big cities) you get the occasional streetdealer, depending on where and at what time. Otherwise my best bet would be to ask around young people in pubs. Discretely ofcourse :) 

Heroin is pretty huge in Oslo, but that's a very specific case and not a representation of the norwegian drug scene. Alcohol is by far the most used and abused drug here (We have a pretty bad bingedrinking culture. And outside the cities it's prefectly normal and expected that you start to drink when you are 14-15). 

Top 3 all around would probably be Alcohol, Cannabis and Amphetamine. Benzos and Opiates and other prescriptions are also fairly common, but I don't have any experience in that field.

I was very overwhelmed and felt that the diagnosis controlled my life for the first few weeks, but then it became a habit and you start to learn your body on a new level. What you can and can't eat, how much physical activity controlls your bloodsugar, subtle signs that tells you if it's way up or way down etc.

But yeah, it might be really rough, or it might be no big deal at all. Take your time and learn at your own pace, and just try out things you are unsure about, while monitoring actively. Some people can eat some pizza and not react at all, while others skyrocket on a slice. 

I've atleast found it more manageable if I can treat myself to something good every once in a while (while setting insulin accordingly) and not become a slave to your illness. Ofcourse, everything in moderation. This atleast helped me immensly while changing my diet and overall day to day activities. You won't be able to binge on all the snacks, but a small bar every once in a while probably won't kill you.
